## Barr's Role in the Pardons

On December 24, 1992, during his final month in office, Bush, on the advice of Barr, pardoned Weinberger, along with five other administration officials who had been found guilty on charges relating to the Iran–Contra affair. ## Lawsuit Details

The Christic Institute filed its lawsuit in May 1986 on behalf of journalists Tony Avirgan and Martha Honey. Avirgan had been seriously wounded in the May 1984 bombing of an Eden Pastora press conference at La Penca, Nicaragua, that killed eight people and injured dozens.

## Defendants List

Among the 30 defendants named were Iran–Contra figures John K. Singlaub, Richard V. Secord, Albert Hakim, and Robert W. Owen; Central Intelligence Agency officials Thomas Clines and Theodore Shackley; Contra leader Adolfo Calero; Medellin cartel leaders Pablo Escobar Gaviria and Jorge Ochoa.

Additional defendants mentioned in the search results include John Hull (a U.S.-born farmer accused of smuggling cocaine and arms) and Felipe Vidal, among others.

## Case Outcome

On June 23, 1988, United States federal judge James Lawrence King of the United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida dismissed the case, and on February 3, 1989, King ordered the Christic Institute to pay $955,000 in attorney's fees and $79,500 in court costs.
